```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)

train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")

# Calculate the four target statistics
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1,
    m2 = R_moment_2,
    m3 = R_moment_3,
    m4 = R_moment_4,

    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    sd_R = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,
    ex_kurt = kurtosis - 3,

    Re = factor(Re),
    Fr = factor(Fr)
  )

# Only use the three input parameters as predictors
X <- train %>%
  select(Re, Fr, St)

# The four required outcomes
Y <- train %>%
  select(R_moment_1, sd_R, skewness, kurtosis)

# Check for invalid values before modeling
summary(Y)
sapply(Y, function(x) sum(!is.finite(x)))

```
```{r}
train %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(R_moment_1, sd_R, skewness, kurtosis),
    names_to = "response",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ response, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of Response Variables",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Frequency"
  )
```

```{r}
# Set up leave-one-out cross-validation
set.seed(325)

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "LOOCV"
)

# Candidate penalty values
# alpha = 0: ridge
# alpha = 1: lasso
# lambda chooses how strongly model penalizes large coefs (this isn't a model param, penalty param). we test out 50 diff penalty values from 10^-4 to 10^2
tune_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = c(0, 1),
  lambda = 10^seq(-4, 2, length.out = 50)
)

# Functiont o fit a ridge/lasso model for one response
fit_regularized <- function(response_name) {

  # Combine predictors with the outcome being predicted
  # X: Re, Fr, St
  # Y: 4 outcomes
  # Y[[response_name]] gets outcome requested by function
  dat <- bind_cols(
    X,
    y = Y[[response_name]]
  )

  # Fit models and select the best settings using LOOCV
  model <- train(
    y ~ .,
    data = dat,
    method = "glmnet",
    trControl = ctrl,
    tuneGrid = tune_grid, # test 100 combos of alpha and lambda
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("center", "scale") # center (subtract mean) and scale (divide by std)
  )

  return(model)
}

# Fit models for all four outcomes
set.seed(325)

# call function for each outcome
models <- lapply(
  names(Y),
  fit_regularized
)

names(models) <- names(Y)

# Extract the selected alpha and lambda for each outcome
best_params <- map_dfr(names(models), function(nm) {
  models[[nm]]$bestTune %>%
    mutate(response = nm)
})

# View selected settings
best_params

# View LOOCV RMSE for every candidate setting
cv_results <- map_dfr(names(models), function(nm) {
  models[[nm]]$results %>%
    mutate(response = nm)
})

cv_results
```
```{r}
cv_results %>%
  group_by(response, alpha) %>%
  slice_min(RMSE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(response, alpha, lambda, RMSE)
```

```{r}
cv_results %>%
```

## Now trying linear regression

```{r}
## Load Data
#| label: packages-data

library(tidyverse)
library(moments)
library(boot)

data <- read_csv("data-train.csv")
```

## Transform Data

```{r}
#| label: transform

#making new variables for our summary stats

#mean = R_moment_1, C_moment_2 is variance, everything else is as commented
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1, m2 = R_moment_2, m3 = R_moment_3, m4 = R_moment_4,

    # central moments
    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,                               # variance
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    # standardized versions
    sd_R     = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,                       # raw kurtosis
    ex_kurt  = kurtosis - 3                               # excess kurtosis
  )

#using a categorical to address infinity
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    Fr = as.factor(Fr),
    Re = as.factor(Re)
  )
```

```{r}
data
```

## Model Testing
```{r}
# Model 1: Linear main effects
m1 <- lm(skewness ~ St + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 2: Log-transformed St
m2 <- lm(skewness ~ log(St) + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 3: Log-transformed skewness, normal St
m3 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ St + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 4: Log-transformed skewness, log-transformed St
m4 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 5: All pairwise interactions, no transformations
m5 <- lm(skewness ~ St * Re + St * Fr + Re * Fr,
         data = data)

# Model 6: All pairwise interactions + three-way interaction
m6 <- lm(skewness ~ St * Re * Fr,
         data = data)

# Model 7: Log(St) + all pairwise interactions
m7 <- lm(skewness ~ log(St) * Re +
                     log(St) * Fr +
                     Re * Fr,
         data = data)

# Model 8: Log(St) + all interactions, including three-way
m8 <- lm(skewness ~ log(St) * Re * Fr,
         data = data)

# Model 9: Log(skewness) + all pairwise interactions
m9 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ St * Re +
                         St * Fr +
                         Re * Fr,
         data = data)

# Model 10: Log(skewness) + all interactions, including three-way
m10 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ St * Re * Fr,
          data = data)

# Model 11: Both logs + all pairwise interactions
m11 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re +
                          log(St) * Fr +
                          Re * Fr,
          data = data)

# Model 12: Both logs + all interactions, including three-way
m12 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re * Fr,
          data = data)

# Interaction between St and Re; Fr stays a main effect
m15 <- lm(skewness ~ St * Re + Fr, data = data)

# Interaction between St and Fr; Re stays a main effect
m16 <- lm(skewness ~ St * Fr + Re, data = data)

# Interaction between Re and Fr; St stays a main effect
m17 <- lm(skewness ~ Re * Fr + St, data = data)

 # Interaction between log(St) and Re
m18 <- lm(skewness ~ log(St) * Re + Fr, data = data)

# Interaction between log(St) and Fr
m19 <- lm(skewness ~ log(St) * Fr + Re, data = data)

# Interaction between Re and Fr
m20 <- lm(skewness ~ Re * Fr + log(St), data = data)

# Interaction between St and Re
m21 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ St * Re + Fr, data = data)

# Interaction between St and Fr
m22 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ St * Fr + Re, data = data)

# Interaction between Re and Fr
m23 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ Re * Fr + St, data = data)

# Interaction between log(St) and Re
m24 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re + Fr, data = data)

# Interaction between log(St) and Fr
m25 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Fr + Re, data = data)

# Interaction between Re and Fr
m26 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ Re * Fr + log(St), data = data)
```


```{r}
models <- list(
  m1 = m1, m2 = m2, m3 = m3, m4 = m4,
  m5 = m5, m6 = m6, m7 = m7, m8 = m8,
  m9 = m9, m10 = m10, m11 = m11, m12 = m12,
  m15 = m15, m16 = m16, m17 = m17,
  m18 = m18, m19 = m19, m20 = m20,
  m21 = m21, m22 = m22, m23 = m23,
  m24 = m24, m25 = m25, m26 = m26
)

# Keep complete observations used by all models
# This assumes St is numeric and Re and Fr are factors
dat <- data[
  complete.cases(data[, c("skewness", "St", "Re", "Fr")]) &
    is.finite(data$skewness) &
    is.finite(data$St),
]

# Make sure log-response models are mathematically valid
if (any(dat$skewness <= 0)) {
  stop("log(skewness) models require all skewness values > 0.")
}

# LOOCV function
run_loocv <- function(model, dat) {

  n <- nrow(dat)
  predictions <- numeric(n)

  # Is the response log-transformed?
  lhs <- paste(deparse(formula(model)[[2]]), collapse = "")
  log_response <- grepl(
    "^log\\s*\\(\\s*skewness\\s*\\)$", lhs
  )

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {

    train <- dat[-i, , drop = FALSE]
    test  <- dat[i, , drop = FALSE]

    # Refit using all observations except the held-out row
    fit <- lm(
      formula(model),
      data = train,
      na.action = na.exclude
    )

    pred <- as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = test))

    if (log_response) {
      # Smearing correction for back-transforming log predictions
      smear <- mean(exp(residuals(fit)), na.rm = TRUE)
      pred <- exp(pred) * smear
    }

    predictions[i] <- pred
  }

  actual <- dat$skewness
  errors <- actual - predictions

  data.frame(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors))
  )
}

# Evaluate every model
cv_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(models, function(m) run_loocv(m, dat))
)

cv_results$model <- rownames(cv_results)
rownames(cv_results) <- NULL

# Put model name first
cv_results <- cv_results[, c("model", "RMSE", "MAE")]

# Sort by lowest RMSE
cv_results <- cv_results[order(cv_results$RMSE), ]

print(cv_results)
```

```{r}
  cex.names = 0.7,
  main = "LOOCV RMSE by Model",
  ylab = "RMSE"
)

# MAE comparison

)
```

## consistency w rest of group - just start w log transform

```{r}
# Model 1: Linear main effects (kept as requested)
m1 <- lm(skewness ~ St + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 2: Both logs, no interactions
m2_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) + Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 3: Both logs + all pairwise interactions
m3_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re +
                           log(St) * Fr +
                           Re * Fr,
           data = data)

# Model 4: Both logs + all interactions, including three-way
m4_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re * Fr,
           data = data)

# Model 5: Both logs + interaction between log(St) and Re
m5_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Re + Fr, data = data)

# Model 6: Both logs + interaction between log(St) and Fr
m6_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ log(St) * Fr + Re, data = data)

# Model 7: Both logs + interaction between Re and Fr
m7_2 <- lm(log(skewness) ~ Re * Fr + log(St), data = data)
```

```{r}
evaluate_model <- function(model, model_name = deparse(substitute(model))) {
  model_summary <- summary(model)

  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    R_squared = model_summary$r.squared,
    Adjusted_R_squared = model_summary$adj.r.squared,
    AIC = AIC(model),
    BIC = BIC(model)
  )
}
```

```{r}
models <- list(
  m1 = m1, m2_2 = m2_2, m3_2 = m3_2, m4_2 = m4_2,
  m5_2 = m5_2, m6_2 = m6_2, m7_2 = m7_2
)


model_comparison <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(models), function(name) {
    evaluate_model(models[[name]], name)
  })
)

print(model_comparison)
```

based on everything, we could either do m4_2 or m7_2. RMSE/MAE/BIC are lower for m7_2 but AIC/adj R^2 are better for m7_2.
